original_value: AbstractThe concept of resilience is commonly used to represent “an ability to adapt to a changing environment and to survive flexibly despite facing difficulties.” This definition of resilience emphasized its aspects of unpredictable responsiveness to external disturbances as well as self-organized phenomena, which seemed to be close to the definition of complex adaptive systems. This article summarizes the technical challenges to consider the implementation of a concept of resilience into systems from a variety of perspectives. Then, challenges to tackle with the resilience to variabilities in production plans, in work quality, in empirical knowledge, in human-automation systems, and in organizations are presented.

result.paraphrase: AbstractThe concept of resilience is often used to mean “the capacity to adapt to a changing environment and survive flexibly in the face of difficulties.” This definition highlights resilience’s unpredictable response to external disturbances, as well as self-organizing behavior, making it seem close to the definition of complex adaptive systems. This article reviews the technical challenges involved in implementing a concept of resilience in systems from several perspectives. It then presents challenges for dealing with variability in production plans, work quality, empirical knowledge, human-automation systems, and organizations.
